features.title: Everything You Need to Know

stages.title: Announcement & MCC
stages.description: The Election Commission of India announces the election dates. The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) comes into effect immediately to ensure a level playing field.
stages.details: The MCC regulates the conduct of political parties and candidates. No new government schemes or projects can be announced that might influence voters.

stages.title: Nomination Filing
stages.description: Candidates file their nomination papers along with affidavits declaring their assets, liabilities, and criminal records (if any).
stages.details: Any Indian citizen over 25 years of age can contest for Lok Sabha. They must deposit a security amount and get proposers from the constituency.

stages.title: Scrutiny & Withdrawal
stages.description: The Returning Officer scrutinizes the nominations. Invalid ones are rejected. Candidates can withdraw their names within a specified period.
stages.details: After the withdrawal deadline, the final list of contesting candidates is published, and election symbols are allocated to independent candidates.

stages.title: Campaigning
stages.description: Political parties and candidates campaign to reach out to voters through rallies, door-to-door visits, and media.
stages.details: Campaigning must stop 48 hours before the end of polling in the respective constituency (known as the silence period).

stages.title: Polling Phases (7 Phases)
stages.description: Voters cast their votes using Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs). For national elections like Lok Sabha, this often happens across multiple phases.
stages.details: The 2024 Lok Sabha elections were held in 7 phases to manage logistics and security across the country's vast geography.

stages.title: Counting of Votes
stages.description: EVMs from all polling stations are brought to secure counting centers. Votes are counted under the supervision of the Returning Officer and candidate agents.
stages.details: The VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) slips are also matched with EVM counts in randomly selected polling stations.

stages.title: Result Declaration & Government
stages.description: Results are officially declared. The party or coalition with a majority (272+ seats for Lok Sabha) is invited by the President to form the government.
stages.details: The newly elected MPs take their oath, and the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers are sworn in to lead the country for the next 5 years.

howToVote.title: How to Vote in India
howToVote.subtitle: Follow these simple steps on election day
howToVote.step1Desc: Bring your EPIC (Electoral Photo Identity Card) or any of the 12 approved alternative documents like Aadhaar, Passport, or Driving License.
howToVote.step2Desc: Locate your assigned polling booth using the voters.eci.gov.in portal or the Voter Helpline App. Your booth number is printed on your Voter Slip.
howToVote.step3Desc: Arrive at the polling station and join the queue. Senior citizens and differently-abled voters get priority access through special queues.
howToVote.step4Desc: Show your ID to the polling officer at Table 1. They will verify your name on the electoral roll and mark your name.
howToVote.step5Desc: The presiding officer will apply indelible ink on the index finger of your left hand — a mark of democratic participation.
howToVote.step6Desc: Press the button next to your chosen candidate's name and symbol on the EVM. A green light and beep confirm your vote. VVPAT slip will appear briefly.
howToVote.note: Remember: Voting is a right, not an obligation. However, every vote counts in shaping India's future!

eligibility.title: Voter Eligibility in India
eligibility.subtitle: Three simple criteria to vote in Indian elections
eligibility.crit1Desc: You must be at least 18 years of age on the qualifying date (1st January of the year of electoral roll revision).
eligibility.crit2Desc: You must be a citizen of India. NRIs can vote if they are enrolled in their home constituency.
eligibility.crit3Desc: You must be ordinarily resident in the constituency where you wish to register.
eligibility.registerDesc: Register online at voters.eci.gov.in using Form 6, or visit your nearest Booth Level Officer (BLO) for offline registration.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything first-time voters need to know

items.q: How old do I need to be to vote in India?
items.a: You must be at least 18 years old on the qualifying date (January 1st of the electoral roll revision year) to register as a voter in India.

items.q: Can I vote without a Voter ID card?
items.a: Yes! Even without an EPIC (Voter ID), you can vote using 12 alternative documents: Aadhaar card, MNREGA job card, Passbooks with photo from Bank/Post Office, Health smart card, Driving License, PAN card, Smart card by RGI, Passport, Pension document with photo, NPR Smart card, Disability certificate, and Official identity documents issued by Central/State government.

items.q: What is NOTA and how does it work?
items.a: NOTA (None of the Above) is an option on the EVM that allows voters to reject all candidates. Press the NOTA button if you don't wish to vote for any candidate. NOTA votes are counted but cannot win an election.

items.q: What is the Model Code of Conduct?
items.a: The Model Code of Conduct (MCC) is a set of guidelines issued by the Election Commission of India to regulate political parties and candidates during elections. It comes into effect from the date of election announcement to the result date.

EVM (Electronic Voting Machine) is a standalone electronic device used in Indian elections since 1982. It consists of a Control Unit (with the polling officer) and a Balloting Unit (in the voting compartment). It is tamper-proof and stores up to 2000 votes.

items.q: Can NRIs vote in Indian elections?
items.a: Yes, NRIs (Non-Resident Indians) can register as overseas electors in their home constituency using Form 6A. However, they must travel back to India to cast their vote in person as postal/proxy voting is not yet available for NRIs.
